content.value_statement: Teams lose visibility when task status, Trello cards, and local files drift apart. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through consistent lifecycle updates.
actual_capabilities: Chooses local task or Trello card workflows based on project setup.
Guides start, progress, block, review, and completion status changes.
Explains hooks for Trello sync, timers, metrics, velocity, and state updates.
Provides validation steps for task format and completion readiness.
Maps local task statuses to expected Trello board lists.
limitations: Requires the PairCoder CLI and the expected project task layout.
Trello workflows require configured credentials and a connected board.
Validation scripts cannot prove implementation quality or product correctness.
Placeholder task IDs and list names must be replaced before real updates.

use_cases.title: Start or Block Work
use_cases.description: Move a task into progress or blocked status while keeping local state and Trello aligned.

use_cases.title: Standardize Completion
use_cases.description: Run readiness checks and complete tasks through the correct local or Trello workflow.

use_cases.title: Maintain Project Visibility
use_cases.description: Add progress comments, update card fields, and keep delivery boards current.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin work on a local task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the managing-task-lifecycle skill to start TASK-123. Choose the correct workflow and report the status change.

prompt_templates.title: Post Progress
prompt_templates.scenario: Share an update on a Trello-linked task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add a progress update for TRELLO-12: API routes are complete and tests are next.

prompt_templates.title: Complete Safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Validate and close a task after implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to validate TASK-123, summarize readiness, and complete the linked Trello card only if checks pass.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile State
prompt_templates.scenario: Fix mismatched local and Trello task status.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare local task status with the Trello workflow, then propose the safest commands to align them.

output_examples.input: Start TASK-245 in a non-Trello project.
output: Changed the task to in progress through the PairCoder CLI.
Reported that hooks should update timers and state files.

output_examples.output: The assistant validates readiness, records a concise completion summary, moves the card to Done, and notes follow-up state updates.

output_examples.input: A task is blocked because the API contract is unclear.
output_examples.output: The assistant marks the task blocked, adds a clear reason, and keeps the board visible for the team.

best_practices: Confirm whether the project uses Trello before changing status.
Run validation checks before completion and report any failures.
Use exact task IDs, card IDs, summaries, and destination lists.
anti_patterns: Marking a task done without checking acceptance criteria.
Running both local and Trello completion flows for the same task.
Using placeholder task IDs or list names in real commands.

faq.question: Does this skill require Trello?
faq.answer: No. It supports local PairCoder tasks, but Trello workflows need a connected board.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: It guides agents to use PairCoder CLI commands for task state changes and validation.

faq.question: What does the validation cover?
faq.answer: It checks task format, status values, acceptance criteria sections, tests, linting, and git status.

faq.question: Can it complete acceptance criteria?
faq.answer: It can guide the completion workflow, but users should verify the work before closing a task.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The skill is prepared for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is it useful outside PairCoder projects?
faq.answer: It is most useful when the PairCoder CLI and expected task files are present.
